table_notes: *Size on disk* is the download. *VRAM (weights)* is what `serve_clef.py` holds on the GPU: the NVFP4 checkpoints are unpacked to BF16 there (transformers has no packed-NVFP4 kernels), so today only INT4 actually saves VRAM, and the NVFP4 files are for engines with native FP4. *Agrees with BF16* is the share of 258 held-out decision questions where the quant picks the same top answer as Cloudflare's BF16 model run through the same code. BF16 against itself under a different expert kernel scores 95.7%, so about 96% is the ceiling. *Decision Index* is the chance-corrected public index from the [Decision Index kit](https://github.com/apolinario/decision-index), edition 0.2.1 (the edition behind Cloudflare's published Clef-Omni results), on our hardware.
eval_method: Parity: 128 held-out records (258 questions; text from ultrachat_200k test_sft in Clef's state/questions schema, about 20% with synthetic image/video/audio, never used for calibration). Each exported quant is loaded through `serve_clef.py` and compared with Cloudflare's BF16 model run through the same code path (grouped experts). We report top-answer agreement and total variation (TV) between the per-option distributions. **Noise floor:** the same BF16 weights run through a different but equally valid expert kernel (eager vs grouped) agree on only 95.7% of these questions (TV 0.028), because many are near-ties. Agreement around 96% and TV near 0.03 therefore means indistinguishable from BF16 at this precision. Benchmarks: the Decision Index reproduction kit, edition 0.2.1, over `/v1/systemone` on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
recommendations: **clef-omni-int4**: any recent GPU when you want the smallest VRAM footprint today; loads in plain transformers. Also the best bet on AMD (ROCm): AutoRound's PyTorch/Triton kernels run there, though we have not tested it.
**clef-omni-nvfp4a16**: Blackwell, or vLLM's Marlin MoE path on older cards; NVFP4 weights with 16-bit activations (higher fidelity than W4A4).
**clef-omni-nvfp4**: Blackwell engines with native FP4 tensor cores (W4A4 is the only variant that can run faster than BF16 there).
**clef-omni** (Cloudflare BF16): the reference, if you have ~70 GB of VRAM.

quants.summary: NVFP4 (W4A4) quantization of [Cloudflare/clef-omni](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-omni) (revision `0db1cd2`) made with NVIDIA ModelOpt 0.47.0. **22.0 GB instead of 70.8 GB.** Only the thinker's MoE experts (about 91% of the loaded weights) are FP4; attention, router, embeddings, `lm_head`, the vision and audio towers and the Clef joint decision head stay BF16.
quants.status: experimental (`max` calibration). Faithful W4A4 replay agrees with BF16 on 92.6% of held-out decisions (TV 0.059) and scores 0.76 points below BF16 on the Decision Index; the INT4 sibling is the better choice for most people.
serving: `serve_clef.py` keeps the FP4 experts packed in VRAM and unpacks each layer just in time for transformers' grouped kernels: about 28 GB on the card (15.3 GiB of expert weights) at about 0.55 s per decision. `--no-packed-nvfp4` unpacks everything at load (about 60 GB, about 0.16 s). By default activations stay BF16; `--simulate-fp4-activations` also rounds expert inputs to NVFP4 exactly as ModelOpt calibrated them (faithful W4A4, several seconds per decision, used for the benchmarks). Native FP4 execution needs an engine with NVFP4 kernels plus a hidden-state path into the Clef head.
quantized: | Part | Precision |
| Thinker MoE experts (48 layers x 128 experts, gate/up/down) | **NVFP4 W4A4**: E2M1 weights in blocks of 16 with FP8 E4M3 block scales + FP32 global scale; FP4 activations |
| Attention, router (`mlp.gate`), embeddings, `lm_head` | BF16 |
| Vision and audio towers | BF16 |
| Clef joint head (`joint_head.safetensors`) | BF16, byte-identical to the original |

quants.summary: INT4 weight-only (W4A16, group size 128, symmetric) quantization of [Cloudflare/clef-omni](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-omni) (revision `0db1cd2`) made with Intel AutoRound 0.16.0 (SignRound, 200 tuning steps per block on Clef-format records). Only the thinker's MoE experts are FP8; attention, router, embeddings, `lm_head`, the vision and audio towers and the Clef joint decision head stay BF16.
serving: `serve_clef.py` keeps the FP8 experts packed in VRAM (FP8 weights plus FP32 tile scales) and dequantizes each layer just in time for transformers' grouped matmul, so the head runs unchanged. transformers 5.10.2 also loads the checkpoint itself (`quant_method: fp8`, dequantized or native FP8 experts), and the format is the one vLLM and SGLang load for Qwen FP8 releases.
quantized: | Part | Precision |
| Thinker MoE experts | **FP8 E4M3 weights**, one FP32 scale per 128x128 block; activations BF16 (or dynamic FP8 per 1x128 group in engines) |
| Attention, router, embeddings, `lm_head`, vision and audio towers | BF16 |
| Clef joint head | BF16, byte-identical to the original |
recipe: `scripts/clef-omni/quant_fp8_block.py`: converts the per-expert BF16 tensors straight from the release shards (no model load, no calibration), using transformers 5.10.2's own block-FP8 math (`Fp8Quantize`: scale = 448/amax per 128x128 tile, round-to-nearest cast), and writes `weight` (F8_E4M3) plus `weight_scale_inv` (F32). Everything else is copied bit-for-bit; talker/code2wav are dropped. CPU-only, streaming, under 1.5 GiB of host RAM.

bench_note: Decision Index 0.2.1 (the edition behind Cloudflare's published Clef-Omni table), run with the public [decision-index kit](https://github.com/apolinario/decision-index) (suite rebuilt and hash-verified against the lab's manifest) over `/v1/systemone` on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell. We score a deterministic stratified sample of 3,000 requests (about 58 per benchmark, `suite sample --n 3000`) rather than all ~150K, so each benchmark carries roughly ±5-7 points of sampling noise; the averages and the paired deltas (both models on the identical questions, `score --reference`) are the reliable signals. The kit's headline index is coverage-adjusted over the full suite, so it is not meaningful on a sample and is not reported.
board_note: Full-suite Decision Index for clef-omni-int4 (every scoreable request, coverage 100%, 0 errors): **56.93** on edition 0.2.1 (raw 66.87; areas: knowledge 49.96, language 54.48, retrieval 58.92, tools 73.38, arts 47.27) and **56.42** on the live 0.3 board (raw 66.84). For orientation on the public board: Cloudflare Clef (Qwen3.8-27B base) 61.21 / 61.71, Jev 57.91 / 57.89, Clef-flash 57.07 (0.2.1). Cloudflare publishes per-benchmark Clef-Omni scores but no Clef-Omni index, so there is no BF16 index to compare directly; the paired 3,000-request sample puts INT4 within 0.13 points of BF16. Run with `serve_clef.py`, which uses Cloudflare's encode_record (it truncates state beyond 64K tokens, where the board's rule counts such rows unsupported).
